title.narrative: Tunisia Social Development Promotion Support Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective of the Tunisia Covid-19 Social Protection Emergency Response Project is to provide cash support to poor and vulnerable households affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and contribute to strengthening the social protection system in Tunisia. The project will support: (i) the GOT's measures to mitigate the COVID-19 impact on poor and low-income households as well as (ii) the AMEN Social program. It was prepared with a view to leverage different sources of funding that are uniquely suited to address specific challenges and support social protection programs. As a result, the proposed activities will be supported by a US$300 million IBRD loan and a US$18 million equivalent grant from the Multi-Donor Trust Fund (MDTF)22. The proposed project includes four components. The first component supports the government's response to mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 crisis and will include financing, in part retroactively, of the AMEN Social PCT and its targeted expansion to support poor households enrolled in the program, and the financing of TCT to support poor and vulnerable households. The second component will support the Family Allowance component of the AMEN Social program with a focus on mitigating the impact of the pandemic on families with children, while protecting their human capital. The third component will support the strengthening of the social protection system to deliver efficient and inclusive programs. The project also includes a Response Component (CERC) with zero funds allocated for the time being, which would allow the government to request a rapid reallocation of project funds to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible emergency or crisis.
The Project objective is to provide cash support to poor and vulnerable households affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and contribute to strengthening the social protection system in Tunisia.

condition.narrative: Section I. F. No later than ninety (90) days after the Effective Date, or such other date as agreed with the Bank, the Borrowershall furnish to the Bank a financial audit in accordance with consistently applied auditing standards acceptable to the Bankregarding the provision of permanent cash transfers under the AMEN Social Program corresponding to the Borrower's Fiscal Year2021.

Section I.A.1.(a)The Borrower shall vest the overall responsibility of the Project on its MoSA and, to this end, shall, throughMoSA:(a) maintain, throughout Project implementation, a Project coordinator supported by a team of professionals (“DeliveryUnit”) to be selected no later than 15 days after the effective Date, or such later date as agreed with the Bank, withqualifications, experience and terms of reference acceptable to the Bank, and responsible for the day-to-day implementation,coordination, monitoring, reporting and evaluation of the Project, all as further described in the Project Operational Manual.

Section I.A.1.(b)No later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed with the Bank, establishand thereafter maintain, throughout Project implementation, the technical committees (“Technical Committees”), with composition andfunctions as further described in the Project Operational Manual, responsible for assisting the Delivery Unit in the technicalimplementation of the Project.

Section I.A.1.(c) no later than sixty (60) days after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed with the Bank, establish andthereafter maintain a Project inter-ministerial steering committee (“Project Steering Committee”) with composition and functions asfurther described in the POM, responsible for the strategic guidance of the Project.

Section I.A.2.(a) No later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, or any later date as agreed with the Bank, prepare aProject Operational Manual in form and substance acceptable to the Bank (“POM”), and (ii) immediately thereafter, implement theProject in accordance with the POM.

Section I.A.2.(a) no later than sixty (60) days after the Effective Date, or any later date as agreed with the Bank, update theProject Operational Manual (“POM”) in form and substance acceptable to the Bank; and (ii) immediately thereafter, implement theProject in accordance with the POM.

Section I.C.1.The Borrower, through the MoSA, shall carry out a verification process at least annually through the GeneralControl of Public Services for the verification of achievement of PBCs which are set forth in the table in Schedule 4 to thisAgreement, and furnish to the Bank not later than sixty (60) days after the verification of compliance of said PBCs, reports on theresults of said verification of compliance process of such scope and in such detail as the Bank shall reasonably request.

title.narrative: Grievances, complaints and inquiries related to the AMEN Social program addressed within the time frame outlined in the project operations manual

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the percentage of grievances on TCTs, FAs, disability allowances, and PCTs received through various channels and resolved in a timely manner, as described in the project operations manual.
Over 590 grievances, complaints, and inquiries were received by BRC (Office of relations with citizens) from January 2025 to June 2025 (381 by mail and 205 directly in BRC offices). 35 percent of written complaints were addressed. 764 complaints were filed with the CGPS, of which 15 percent were addressed.
A calculation error resulted in an overestimation of the reported value for the previous period.

title.narrative: Children 0-5 years old of households receiving Family Allowance among all eligible children 0-5 years old enrolled in AMEN Social registry

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the total number of children aged 0-5 receiving the FA among all children aged 0-5 enrolled in the AMEN Social Registry. The gap to achieving 100 percent is explained by the fact that part of children aged 0-5 enrolled in the AMEN Social Registry belongs to households not meeting FA eligibility criteria checked through cross-checks with administrative databases (such as CNSS and CNRPS to check revenues or with ATTT to check vehicle property). Therefore, these households are excluded from FA benefits.

title.narrative: Electronic dashboard to monitor payments disbursment and cash-out

comment.narrative: This indicator monitors the electronic Dashboard setup to monitor disbursements of PCT programs under the AMEN Social. The WB TA on the G2P initiative supports MoSA and CNSS to provide a benchmark on the international experience of a dashboard to monitor payments, disbursements, and cash-out; a proof of concept (POC) was developed in 2024; however, data exchange with the Tunisian Poste is required to further roll out this POC.

title.narrative: Establishment of an integrated and functional delivery system to provide social protection services efficiently in climate vulnerable areas

comment.narrative:
This indicator monitors the implementation of a database, including the geolocation of beneficiaries in the areas at risk, ensuring that the payment systems take into account potential disruption from a potential risk.
Among 868,172 social surveys conducted, about 500,000 include geolocation of beneficiaries. The gap is due to a technical issue in the geolocation feature during a period that disabled registration of GPS coordinates through mobile tablets used by social workers to conduct an on-field survey.

title.narrative: Manual data cross-checks of households enrolled in the AMEN Social Registry reduced

comment.narrative: Subject to confirmation by the CGSP of the achievement of this PBC during its mission on November 17, 2025: An automatic data cross-check platform integrated into the AMEN management information system was implemented in March 2024, enabling data cross-checks with Social funds (CNSS and CNRPS) as well as the vehicle property registry (ATTT). Additional data cross-checks with the civil registry and social identifier registry (CRES) were implemented in July 2024, enabling the reduction of manual entries in the AMEN Social registry and identification of registered individuals. Additional data cross-checks with the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Higher Education are expected to be implemented in 2025.

title.narrative: Households receiving the AMEN Social Permanent Cash Transfers (PCTs) through the new selection process

comment.narrative: Target not yet achieved. As of November 2025, 383,192 households received PCTs. Of these, over 220,000 are potentially eligible according to the new circular, subject to verification by the digital regional commissions (85,930 have already been verified, and 135,237 are pending verification). MoSA is actively implementing an action plan to expedite the recertification process of PCT beneficiaries, aiming to achieve PBC 1a (114,000 eligible households targeted using the new selection process) by December 2025.
